subject: School Committee Compensation and Migrant Shelter
overview: The Council approved a two-year phased compensation increase for the School Committee and discussed the state's plan to open a temporary emergency shelter for migrant families in Medford. They also reviewed a report on 2023 municipal election errors and referred various pro-democracy reforms to committee for further study.

items.title: Approval of Records
items.summary: Approved the records of the January 9, 2024, regular meeting.

items.title: Report of the Committee of the Whole on School Committee Compensation
items.summary: Accepted the January 17, 2024, committee report regarding school committee compensation.

items.title: Council Communications and Website Updates
items.summary: Referred resolutions to modernize council communication outreach and update the city website to the Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee.

items.title: Proposed Temporary Shelter on Riverside Avenue
items.summary: Discussed a state proposal for a temporary emergency shelter at 400 Riverside Avenue and approved a motion for a neighborhood robocall once a public meeting is scheduled. Residents and councilors raised concerns regarding public health, school capacity, infrastructure, and the lack of communication from the state government.

items.title: 2023 Municipal Election Process Errors and Accountability Report
items.summary: Reviewed a report detailing errors in the 2023 municipal election and referred the matter to the Governance Committee to address staffing shortages and procedural improvements. The discussion focused on delays in tabulating unofficial results and the inadvertent zeroing of memory cards at several precincts.

items.title: Withdrawn Resolution on Communication Platforms
items.summary: Paper 24-018 was withdrawn by the sponsor.

items.title: School Committee Compensation Increases
items.summary: Approved a two-year phased compensation increase for School Committee members effective July 1, 2024, and July 1, 2025. Councilors described the move as a compromise following 24 years without a salary adjustment for the body.

items.title: Pro-Democracy Reforms Study
items.summary: Referred a series of reforms including public financing, ranked choice voting, and non-citizen voting for green card holders to the Governance Committee for study.

items.title: Council and School Committee Blended Salary Resolution
items.summary: Ruled a resolution to lower council pay out of order because state law prohibits salary reductions or increases for councilors from taking effect during the year they are voted.
